title: Al-Mu'id, the Restorer
tomorrow: a prophet asks to see the dead brought to life. what does he get?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Mubdi': the first move is His, and bismillah borrows it. The line: he begins. The question was what comes after the beginning. And it's the end of the week, so six lines are coming back with it.

The streak is gone. The little flame on the app has gone gray, and the counter says zero. Right there, it's tempting to quietly delete the app. Here's the next line after yesterday's verse, from Surah ar-Rum in Pickthall's words: "He it is Who produceth creation, then reproduceth it, and it is easier for Him." He begins, and then He brings back. Today's Name: Al-Mu'id, the Restorer.
screen: `THE FLAME GONE GRAY.` → `HE BEGINS, THEN BRINGS BACK.` → `AL-MU'ID.`

segments.voice: The tradition reads this pair, beginning and bringing back, first about creation itself: the One who made it once will bring it back after death. And the same idea of return runs through a word the tradition uses every day, tawba, repentance, which at heart means turning back. Here's the hadith worth telling a friend. The Prophet, peace be upon him, described a man in the desert whose camel wanders off with all his food and water. He gives up and lies down to wait for the end. He wakes, and the camel is standing beside him. Allah, the hadith says, is more pleased with a servant who turns back than that man is with his camel. A return, celebrated, not scolded. Now the week, looking back. His strength, at the well. Firm, small and steady. Friend, a guardian who stays near. Praised, in every state, even through tears. Counted, every good thing. He begins, the first move. And today, he brings back. The streak broke. The door didn't.
screen: `PRODUCETH, THEN REPRODUCETH.` · `TAWBA: TURNING BACK.` · `THE CAMEL STANDING THERE.` · `SIX LINES, ONE WEEK.` · then, large: `HE BRINGS BACK.`

segments.voice: Choose one practice that slipped lately: a nightly page, a prayer, a walk, a call you used to make. Don't start over from the beginning. Do one minute of it now, right where you left off, and sit the rest of the two minutes with it back in your hands.
screen: `ONE PRACTICE THAT SLIPPED.` · `PICK UP WHERE YOU LEFT OFF.`

segments.voice: Al-Mu'id. The Restorer: the one who brings creation back, and keeps the door open for anyone turning back.
The line to keep: he brings back, so a gap is never the last page. Week done; see you in the morning.

howItsDone: Muslims speak of tawba, turning back to Allah, as a door that stays open; Al-Mu'id, the Restorer, is recited beside Al-Mubdi', the Originator, in the list of the Names.

the Name is about bringing back, not starting over: pick up where you stopped.
in the hadith, Allah is more pleased with a servant's return than a lost man with his found camel

fork.setup: your friend stopped going to the gym for a month and is embarrassed to go back because the front desk 'will notice.' what does the camel story suggest?
options: go back; in the story, the return gets the welcome, not the gap.
wait until she's fit enough again that nobody can tell.
sign up somewhere new where nobody knows her history.
fork.reveal: the hadith pictures joy at a return, bigger than a lost man's joy at his camel. the story is about God and His servants, but the shape fits: coming back is the good news.

original.note: Arabic: the Restorer, the one who brings back; recited right after Al-Mubdi' in the list of the Names.

trapdoor: what you thought: God puts broken things back exactly as they were.
what it means: the one who brings creation back, and whose door stays open to anyone turning back.
what a scholar hears: 30:27 and 10:4 pair beginning with bringing back; tawba as return; the lost camel (Sahih al-Bukhari 6309).
guess: the Restorer, who brings back what was
the Rewinder who erases what happened
the Keeper who never lets anything go

chat.says: haven't read my nightly page since dadi's surgery. almost a week. start over at page one?
options: No restart. Open to the page where you stopped; coming back is the point.
Wait until Dadi's better so you can do it properly again.
Start at page one. After a gap, the old pages don't really count.
chat.meaning: Al-Mu'id brings back, and tawba means turning back. The man who finds his camel doesn't start a new trip.
